posts.author: DrOutlier
posts.post_subject: Holography probably not like riding a bike.
posts.content_md:
8) It's been awhile since I made a hologram. Come to think, it was near the end of the last century. Even then I only spent a few months making holograms. I should probably start off simple again.

Today I finished dusting off the huge plank of wood I once shot a beam of light over. Most of the equipment has survived the dry California storage.

Then, I realized I still need to get new development chemicals and plates. Maybe I should also try film.

I also need to get Skype now to really be in this group. If I wait a month the 5% discount should cover the Skype expense.

Back to work...

posts.topic_title: Holography probably not like riding a bike.
posts.author: Tom B.
posts.post_subject: Holography probably not like riding a bike.
posts.content_md: Forget film until you have built up your confidence enough to survive the inevitable disappointments with variable film quality and stabilization problems. Plates are much easier to work with and the results when good (say with BB-plates) are much more satisfying than film at present.

posts.content_md:
8) It's just an excuse to justify an internet phone. One of my long term goals is to digitize my whole life. I've converted my audio tape collection to .mp3s and .wavs. I am converting my VHS tapes to digital .vobs and recording TV on the computer. It's just easier and memory keeps on getting cheaper. When holographic memory storage is at CompUSA I'll be first in line.

According to [http://www.worldtimezone.com/wtz-names/wtz-emt.html](http://www.worldtimezone.com/wtz-names/wtz-emt.html) EMT is Norway time so when it's 10:30 saturday morning in Oslo it's 1:30 am in Los Angeles, right?

When will the world learn to use beat time?

Have a good dash.
